results.name: Janet Louise Harwood
results.justification: My propensity is 4, because I like the idea of a ready-to-drink gazpacho as a convenient, vegetable-forward option — it fits my habit of keeping prepared soups on hand for low-energy days and I enjoy mild, savory breakfasts and lunches. I would buy it provided the bottle lists a low-sodium recipe, isn't overly spicy, and is reasonably priced (or from a local maker I trust). It's especially appealing in warmer months or as a light lunch with whole-grain crackers. If it were very high in salt or the flavor too sharp, I'd be less likely to repurchase, but I would certainly try it once.

results.name: Stephen Michael Donnelly
results.justification: Very unlikely but not impossible. Reason: I value home-cooked soups and stews that I can reheat and control for ingredients; I’m skeptical of processed convenience items with long ingredient lists or preservatives. A bottled cold soup would only tempt me in hot weather if it came from a trusted local maker, had a short, recognisable ingredient list (tomatoes, cucumbers, peppers, olive oil, vinegar, salt), and was reasonably priced. Otherwise I’d prefer to make my own or buy from a deli that makes it fresh.

results.name: Warren Ellis Gentry
results.justification: My propensity is 2 — very unlikely, but not impossible. First, I'm a country fella who prefers warm, slow-cooked dishes and home-made staples; cold blended soup isn't part of my regular meals. Second, when I want something like that I'd sooner make a pitcher from garden tomatoes or buy it from a local vendor I trust than reach for a bottled product with mystery ingredients. Third, I might try a bottle once in the heat of summer out of curiosity, especially if it's local and the label is honest about ingredients and price, but I wouldn't buy it regularly. So: 2.

results.name: Evan McAllister
results.justification: I'd maybe buy ready-to-drink gazpacho but it depends. I like fresh veg-forward food and would try it on a hot day or when I'm short on time, especially if it's from a local maker, bottled in glass, reasonably priced, and tastes like real tomatoes/peppers (not overly sweet or canned). I usually prefer to make things at home, and Noah probably wouldn't eat it, so it wouldn't be a regular family staple — more of an occasional convenience or summer treat. If the flavor profile included a little heat or tang, that'd increase the chances.

results.name: Rosa María Castañeda
results.justification: I prefer hot, familiar dishes and simple snacks I know how to trust; a bottled cold Spanish soup feels a bit unfamiliar and like a novelty to me. I worry about price, preservatives, and portion size. I might try one small bottle if it were cheap or Mimi recommended it on a hot day, but I probably would not buy it regularly. Mira, that’s honest — convenient could win me over sometimes, but not often.

results.name: Erin Michelle Dalton
results.justification: My propensity is 3, because while the flavors (tomato, cucumber, olive oil, lemon) line up well with what I like and it would be appealing in warmer months, Iu0002m cautious about ready-to-drink bottles. I would want a clear ingredient list, modest sodium, and reasonable price. If itu0002s sold refrigerated, clearly labeled, and priced like a light lunch or substantial snack, Iu0002d consider buying it occasionally (especially in summer). Iu0002m not an automatic buyer of novel packaged foods, so Iu0002d say u0002maybeu0002 — open to trying if the packaging and price look honest.

results.name: Anthony James Holloway
results.justification: My propensity is 3 — maybe I'd buy it. Here's why: I ain't against trying new, convenient foods, and a chilled gazpacho sounds all right on a hot day, but it's not the kind of filling, meat-centered thing my family usually eats. If y'all put it in a small, inexpensive bottle (say under a few dollars), labeled plainly with simple ingredients and sold chilled in the supermarket, I'd pick one up now and then for myself as a refreshing snack. I wouldn't buy it for a family dinner or as a regular staple unless the price and portion made sense. Things that'd make me more likely: a sampler, a sale, or a familiar brand doing a mild-flavored version. Things that'd make me less likely: high price, fancy packaging that makes it seem expensive, or a flavor that's too vinegary or spicy. Hope that helps — I can also give y'all my self-intro and top-10 interests if you still need that.

results.name: Marjorie Keating
results.justification: I’m cautious about new food products and I watch my salt, so I’d only try it if the flavor sounded mild and the label said low-sodium and simple ingredients. I’d be more likely to buy one in warm weather as a small, refreshing treat, especially if it was a single-serving bottle and I could sample it first or a neighbor recommended it. If it tasted too acidic, raw, or spicy, or if it was pricey for the size, I’d pass. In short — possible in summer under the right conditions, otherwise unlikely.
